hospitals.affiliated_university: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (UNC School of Medicine)
hospitals.description: The state's public academic children's hospital sits inside UNC Medical Center on the UNC-Chapel Hill campus, sharing a building complex with the N.C. Women's, N.C. Cancer and neurosciences hospitals. It cares for patients from birth to age 21 from every corner of North Carolina, with 158 beds that include a 20-bed PICU and a 58-bed Newborn Critical Care Center. It is one of only three Level I pediatric trauma centers in the state, so the acuity mix is high and transfers arrive from community hospitals across central and eastern NC. The campus is a short drive from Durham and about 30 minutes from Raleigh, in a college town with strong schools and a walkable downtown.
highlights: 158 pediatric beds; 20-bed PICU; 58-bed Newborn Critical Care Center
Level I pediatric trauma center, one of three in North Carolina
Teaching hospital of the UNC School of Medicine
Parent UNC Medical Center has roughly 916 to 932 beds and is a Level I adult trauma center
Closest major children's hospital to family in Chapel Hill

hospitals.affiliated_university: Duke University (School of Medicine, School of Nursing)
hospitals.description: Duke's children's hospital occupies part of the Duke University Hospital campus on Erwin Road in Durham, next to the university's West Campus and the Duke medical and nursing schools. It has about 151 beds and includes both a pediatric ICU and a neonatal ICU, serving as a quaternary referral center for children from across the Southeast. The parent hospital opened in 1930, is a Level I trauma center with more than 1,000 beds, and was named the best hospital in North Carolina by U.S. News in 2024. Durham is a mid-sized, fast-growing city about 15 minutes from Chapel Hill and 25 minutes from Raleigh.
highlights: About 151 pediatric beds with PICU and NICU
Inside Duke University Hospital, a 1,062-bed Level I trauma center opened in 1930
Duke University Hospital ranked best hospital in North Carolina by U.S. News (2024)
Hospital school since 1959, run with Durham Public Schools
Academic home of Duke School of Medicine and School of Nursing
hospitals.notes: 15 minutes from Chapel Hill. PICU bed count, NICU level and peds ED details were not stated on pages read this session; peds_ed is set true based on Duke's academic children's emergency service but is unconfirmed. Duke is not listed among North Carolina's three Level I pediatric trauma centers (UNC, Levine, Brenner). Partner in the planned NC Children's campus in Apex with UNC Health.

hospitals.description: WakeMed's children's hospital is part of the system's flagship Raleigh campus on New Bern Avenue, east of downtown Raleigh. The campus runs two separate 24-hour emergency departments, one of them only for children, plus a children's intensive care unit and a Level IV neonatal ICU with a 48-bed nursery. The Raleigh campus is a Level I trauma center and the busiest acute care site in Wake County, so pediatric volume is large and growing with the county. WakeMed is a private not-for-profit system that started as Memorial Hospital of Wake County in 1961.
highlights: Dedicated 24-hour children's emergency department
Level IV NICU (48-bed nursery) and children's ICU
Raleigh campus is a Level I trauma center
WakeMed is one of seven Harvard developmental training sites
Current WakeMed postings include NNP and PNP neonatology roles in Raleigh
hospitals.notes: About 35 minutes from Chapel Hill. The children's hospital bed count and PICU size were not stated on pages read this session. The Level I designation is the campus (adult) trauma center; WakeMed is not among the three Level I pediatric trauma centers named on Wikipedia. WakeMed's job board is server-rendered and showed 294 NP-keyword results, including PNP and NNP neonatology roles, on 2026-10-19.

hospitals.description: WakeMed's second full-service hospital serves Cary, Apex and the fast-growing western side of Wake County from a campus on Kildaire Farm Road. It opened in 1991 as Western Wake Medical Center and is listed at about 208 licensed beds, with a Level III trauma designation. It offers emergency, surgical and women's services for a largely suburban population and transfers higher-acuity children to the Raleigh campus. Cary is about 25 minutes from Chapel Hill, which makes this one of the closest suburban hospitals to the family.

hospitals.description: A 61-bed WakeMed hospital in north Raleigh on Falls of Neuse Road, serving North Raleigh, Wake Forest and the northern suburbs. It grew out of the WakeMed North Healthplex, built on land that was once part of the Pullen plantation. The hospital provides emergency care, surgery and maternity services and relies on the Raleigh campus for pediatric admissions and intensive care. The area is suburban, about 40 minutes from Chapel Hill.
